newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $63, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Wednesday were bid at $63.00 per cwt, steady with Tuesday's sales, but owners were passing and pricing cattle at $64.00 to $65.00, feedlot sources said.
Tuesday's sales totalled over 30,000 head in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and 20,000 to 25,000 in Kansas, the sources estimated.
Feedlot cattle prices were pressured by lackluster beef sales this week and adequate near-term cattle supplies, several feedlot managers said.
A few owners indicated they would wait until next week to sell by virtue of their higher asking levels.
"When you got bids at $63.00 and offers at $65.00, the owner is basically saying he won't trade," accoding to one Kansas feedlot operator.
Trades at $63.00 were creating more losses than profits for the bulk of owners, the operator said.
Those cattle not sold probably were not well finished and could use extra days on feed as owners hold out for higher prices, sources said.
